description: Neutral tone: 300-word incident summary stress test

request.selection:
Incident Summary – April 19 2026

At 14:32 UTC our monitoring system triggered a P1 alert for elevated error rates on the payments service. The on-call engineer acknowledged the alert within 4 minutes and began triaging. Initial investigation pointed to increased latency on database queries in the checkout flow, specifically the inventory lock table which was showing wait times of over 800ms per transaction.

At 14:48 UTC the team identified a query that had regressed after the 14:10 deploy. A recent migration had removed a composite index on (user_id, product_id) in the inventory_locks table, causing full table scans under load. The payments service degraded because checkout transactions were timing out waiting for the lock query to complete.

Mitigation began at 14:55 UTC by re-adding the index via a hotfix migration script applied directly to the primary database. The index build completed in approximately 6 minutes. Error rates began recovering at 15:03 UTC and returned to baseline by 15:11 UTC. Total customer-visible impact window was 39 minutes.

Root cause: the migration in PR-2847 removed the composite index as part of a schema cleanup without a corresponding load test to validate query performance at production traffic levels. The code review process did not catch the performance implication.

Action items: add a required performance review step to the database migration checklist, introduce an automated index coverage check in CI, and require staging load tests for any migration touching tables with over 1 million rows. Owner: infrastructure team. Target completion: May 3 2026.
